newsitem.title: NORWAY: Former U.N. mediator resigns from Norway cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Former U.N. mediator resigns from Norway cabinet.

text.p: Former Middle East mediator Terje Roed-Larsen announced on Wednesday his resignation from the Norwegian government amid a scandal over a share-option scheme dating back to 1986.

The Minister for National Planning quit his post following allegations that he had not told the whole story about a 600,000-crown share-option profit he made 10 years ago while a marketing director at fisheries company Fideco AS.
"Today I have offered to step down as cabinet minister out of consideration for the government's position as well as my own situation," Larsen said.

His announcement followed a call earlier in the day from Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland for a quick political solution to the snowballing scandal, which had become a burden for the Labour minority government.
On Tuesday night Norwegian television suggested that Roed-Larsen altered key dates on documents covering the 1986 share deal for tax purposes. The matter is being investigated by tax authorites.

Roed-Larsen, 48, quit as special United Nations envoy to the Middle East a month ago to head the newly created portfolio for national planning, a key ministry in Jagland's 18-member cabinet which took office in October.
